1896.subject: Zoology
1896.text:
Some of the steps of DNA fingerprinting are given below. Identify their correct sequence from the options given.
A. Electrophoresis of DNA fragments
B. Hybridisation with DNA probe
C. Digestion of DNA by restriction endonucleases
D. Autoradiography
E. Blotting ofDNA fragmentstonitrocellulose membrane
1896.sol:
The technique of DNA fingerprinting involves following steps:
(i) Isolation of DNA from sample cell.
(ii) Amplification of DNA using polymerase chain reaction (PCR), (if DNA is less in amount).
(iii) Digestion of this DNA by restriction endonucleases (C).
(iv) These DNA fragments are electrophoresed in agarose gel. These fragments can be visualised using EtBr-UV system (A).
(v) Separated DNA fragments are transferred to nitrocellulose membrane using Southern Blotting (E).
(vi) Probing for VNTRs is done using labelled DNA probes (B).
(vii)The hybridised fragment can be detected by autoradiography (D).

2085.subject: Zoology
2085.text:
Starting from the maximum, arrange the following male reproductive accessory organs in the correct order, based on the amount of secretion poured into urethra.
(i) Prostrate gland
(ii) Seminal vesicle
(iii) Bulbourethral gland
2085.sol: Seminal vesicles produce an alkaline secretion which forms $60 \%$ of the volume of semen. The secretion of the seminal vesicles contains fructose, prostaglandins, citrate, inositol, and clotting proteins. Prostate gland produces a milky and slightly alkaline secretion which forms $25 \%$ of the volume of semen. It possesses calcium, phosphate, bicarbonate, enzymes prefibrolysin, clotting enzymes, and prostaglandins. Bulbourethral glands or Cowper's glands also secrete an alkaline fluid which neutralizes acids from urine in the urethera. Their secretion contributes the least to semen but is very important.

2233.subject: Zoology
2233.text: Some students, during a study, caught, marked and released 80 fishes in a pond. Later 100 fishes were caught at random. Among these 40 were found to be marked. What is the approximate number of fishes in the pond?
2233.sol:
According to Petersons Mark and Recapture Method, the population (P) is given by

P=m(r+u) / r

where $m=$ number of marked fishes
$r=$ number of marked fishes recaptured
$u=$ number of unmarked fishes captured
Here,

$\begin{aligned}$m & =80 \\
r & =40 \\
u & =(100-40) \\
& =60 \\
P & =$\mathrm{m}(\mathrm{r}+\mathrm{u})$/ $\mathrm{r}$\\
& =$\frac{80(40+60)}{40}$\\
P & =200
\end{aligned}

Here $\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{C} 2, \mathrm{Q}=2 \mathrm{ac}, \mathrm{R}=\mathrm{Q}^2\therefore \quad \mathrm{P}+\mathrm{Q}+\mathrm{R}=\mathrm{C}^2-2 \mathrm{ac}+\mathrm{a}^2=\mathrm{a}^2+\mathrm{c}^2-2 \mathrm{ac}=(\mathrm{a}-\mathrm{C})$

16522.text: A body cools down from $52.5^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}$ to $47.5^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}$ in $5 \mathrm{ min}$ and from $47.5^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}$ to $42.5^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}$ in $7.5 \mathrm{ min}$. Then, the temperature of the surroundings is
16522.sol:
Given that, for first condition,
Initial temperature, $T_1=52.5^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}$
Final temperature, $T_2=47.5^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}$
Average temperature, $T_{\mathrm{av}}=\frac{T_1+T_2}{2}$
=$\frac{525+47.5}{2}=$50^{{}^{\circ}} $\mathrm{C}$For second condition,
Initial temperature, $T_1=47.5^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}$
Final temperature, $T_2=42.5^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}$
Average temperature, $T_{\mathrm{av}}=\frac{T_1+T_2}{2}$
=$\frac{47.5+42.5}{2}=$45^{{}^{\circ}} $\mathrm{C}$Let $T_0$ be the temperature of surroundings. Now, using expression of rate of cooling,

R=$\frac{\Delta T}{\Delta t}=-$K$\left(T_{\mathrm{av}$}-T_0\right)

Substituting the values in above equation from lst and 2 nd conditions, we get

$\frac{T_1-T_2}{t_1}=-$K$\left(T_{\mathrm{av}$}-T_0\right)

$\frac{52.5-47.5}{5}=-$K$\left($50-T_0\right)...(i)

Similarly, $\frac{47.5-42.5}{7.5}=-K\left(45-T_0\right)...(ii)$
Dividing Eq. (i) by Eq. (ii), we get

$\begin{aligned}$$\frac{\frac{52.5-47.5}{5}}{\frac{47.5-42.5}{7.5}}$& =$\frac{-K\left(50-T_0\right)}{-K\left(45-T_0\right)}$\\
\Rightarrow \quad $\frac{5}{5} \times \frac{7.5}{5}$& =$\frac{50-T_0}{45-T_0} \Rightarrow \frac{3}{2}=\frac{50-T_0}{45-T_0}$\\
T_0 & =35^{{}^{\circ}} $\mathrm{C}
\end{aligned}$Hence, the temperature of surroundings is $35^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}$.

Area of cross-section of steel wire,

$T = \dfrac{1}{4} \times \text{stress} \times \text{area of cross-section}$

$= \dfrac{1}{4} \times 2. 2 \times {10}^{8} \times 4 \times {10}^{- 4}$

$= 2. 2 \times {10}^{4}Nm^{- 2}$

If $f$ be the maximum upward acceleration of the elevator, then

$T = m \left(g + f\right)$

$2. 2 \times {10}^{4} =1000 \left(10 + f\right)$

$⇒ f = 12ms^{- 2}$

20445.subject: Chemistry
20445.text: Which of the following statements is incorrect for $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}_2$ structure?
options: It has an open book structure.
It $\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{O}$ bond length is 145.8 and $\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{H}$ is 98.8.
20445.sol: The structure of hydrogen peroxide ($\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}_2$) is non-planar and is commonly described as an open book structure. In the gaseous phase, the dihedral angle between the two O-H planes is approximately $111.5^{{}^{\circ}}$, not $180^{{}^{\circ}}$. A dihedral angle of $180^{{}^{\circ}}$ would imply a planar structure, which is not the case for $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}_2$. The $\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{O}$ bond length in $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}_2$ is $145.8$ pm and the $\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{H}$ bond length is $98.8$ pm. The dihedral angle (angle between the two planes containing the O-H bonds) in the solid state is $90.2^{{}^{\circ}}$. Since the dihedral angle is not $180^{{}^{\circ}}$, the statement that its dihedral angle is $180^{{}^{\circ}}$ is incorrect. Answer: Its dihedral angle is $180^{{}^{\circ}}$.

21330.text: $The order of the differential equation \dfrac{d}{d x}\left[\left(\dfrac{d y}{d x}\right)^3\right]=0$ is
21330.sol:
The given differential equation is $\dfrac{d}{dx}\left[\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^3\right] = 0$.

Applying the chain rule to the derivative, we have $3\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2 \cdot \dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = 0$.

The order of a differential equation is defined as the order of the highest derivative present in the equation.

In this equation, the highest derivative is $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}$, which is a second-order derivative.

Therefore, the order of the differential equation is $2$.

Answer: $2$

21596.subject: Mathematics
21596.text: The solution of the differential equation $e^{-x}(y+1) d y+\left(\cos ^{2} x-\sin 2 x\right) y(d x)=0$ subjected to the condition that $y=1$, when $x=0$ is
21596.sol:
Given, differential equation is
$\begin{aligned}
& e^{-x}(y+1) d y+\left(\cos ^{2} x-\sin 2 x\right) y d x=0 \\
\Rightarrow &\left(\frac{y+1}{y}\right) d y+e^{x}\left(\cos ^{2} x-\sin 2 x\right) d x=0 \\
\Rightarrow &\left(1+\frac{1}{y}\right) d y+\left(e^{x} \cos ^{2} x-e^{x} \sin 2 x\right) d x=0 \\
\Rightarrow & d(y+\log y)+d\left(e^{x} \cos ^{2} x\right)=0
\end{aligned}$
On integrating above equation, we get
$\begin{aligned}
&y+\log y+e^{x} \cos ^{2} x=c \\
&\text{ At } y(0)=1 \\
&\Rightarrow 1+0+e^{0} \cdot 1=c \Rightarrow c=2
\end{aligned}$
Hence, required solution is
$y+\log y+e^{x} \cos ^{2} x=2$

21666.subject: Mathematics
21666.sol:
The given limit is of the form $1^{\infty}$. We use the formula $\lim_{x \rightarrow \infty} (f(x))^{g(x)} = e^{\lim_{x \rightarrow \infty} g(x)(f(x)-1)}$.

Here, $f(x) = 1 + \dfrac{a}{x} + \dfrac{b}{x^2}$ and $g(x) = 2x$.

The limit becomes $e^{\lim_{x \rightarrow \infty} 2x \left(1 + \dfrac{a}{x} + \dfrac{b}{x^2} - 1\right)} = e^{\lim_{x \rightarrow \infty} 2x \left(\dfrac{a}{x} + \dfrac{b}{x^2}\right)}$.

Simplifying the expression inside the exponent:

$\lim_{x \rightarrow \infty} 2x \left(\dfrac{ax + b}{x^2}\right) = \lim_{x \rightarrow \infty} \dfrac{2ax^2 + 2bx}{x^2} = \lim_{x \rightarrow \infty} \left(2a + \dfrac{2b}{x}\right) = 2a$.

We are given that the limit is $e^2$, so $e^{2a} = e^2$.

Equating the exponents, $2a = 2$, which gives $a = 1$.

The value of $b$ does not affect the limit as $\lim_{x \rightarrow \infty} \dfrac{2b}{x} = 0$ for any finite $b$.

Therefore, $a = 1$ and $b$ can be any real number.

Answer: $a=1, b \in \mathbb{R}$

22109.subject: Mathematics
22109.text: A straight line makes positive intercepts on the coordinate axes whose sum is 5. If the line passes through the point $P(-3,4)$ then the equation of a line is
22109.sol:
Let the intercepts of the line on the x-axis and y-axis be $a$ and $b$ respectively. The equation of the line in intercept form is $\dfrac{x}{a} + \dfrac{y}{b} = 1$.

Given that $a + b = 5$, we have $b = 5 - a$. Substituting this into the equation, we get $\dfrac{x}{a} + \dfrac{y}{5 - a} = 1$.

Since the line passes through the point $P(-3, 4)$, we substitute $x = -3$ and $y = 4$ into the equation:

$\dfrac{-3}{a} + \dfrac{4}{5 - a} = 1$

Multiplying by $a(5 - a)$, we get $-3(5 - a) + 4a = a(5 - a)$.

$-15 + 3a + 4a = 5a - a^2$

$a^2 + 2a - 15 = 0$

Factoring the quadratic equation: $(a + 5)(a - 3) = 0$.

Since the intercepts are positive, $a = 3$. Then $b = 5 - 3 = 2$.

Substituting $a = 3$ and $b = 2$ into the intercept form equation: $\dfrac{x}{3} + \dfrac{y}{2} = 1$.

Multiplying by 6, we get $2x + 3y = 6$.

Answer: $2 x+3 y=6$

22321.subject: Mathematics
22321.text: If $x, y$ and $z$ are non-zero real numbers and $\mathrm{a}=x \hat{i}+2 \hat{j}, \mathrm{b}=\hat{y} \hat{j}+3 \hat{k}$ and $\mathrm{c}=x \hat{i}+y \hat{j}+z \hat{k}$ are such that $\mathrm{a} \times \mathrm{b}=z \hat{i}-3 \hat{j}+\hat{k}$, then $[\mathrm{a b} \mathrm{c}]$ is equal to
22321.sol:
Given vectors $\mathrm{a} = x\hat{i} + 2\hat{j}$, $\mathrm{b} = y\hat{j} + 3\hat{k}$, and $\mathrm{c} = x\hat{i} + y\hat{j} + z\hat{k}$.

Calculate the cross product $\mathrm{a} \times \mathrm{b}$:
$\mathrm{a} \times \mathrm{b} = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} \text{ and } \hat{j} \text{ and } \hat{k} \\ x \text{ and } 2 \text{ and } 0 \\ 0 \text{ and } y \text{ and } 3 \end{vmatrix} = \hat{i}(6 - 0) - \hat{j}(3x - 0) + \hat{k}(xy - 0) = 6\hat{i} - 3x\hat{j} + xy\hat{k}$.

Given $\mathrm{a} \times \mathrm{b} = z\hat{i} - 3\hat{j} + \hat{k}$, compare the components:
$z = 6$, $-3x = -3 \Rightarrow x = 1$, and $xy = 1$.

Since $x = 1$ and $xy = 1$, we get $y = 1$.

The scalar triple product $[\mathrm{a} \mathrm{b} \mathrm{c}]$ is defined as $(\mathrm{a} \times \mathrm{b}) \cdot \mathrm{c}$.

$[\mathrm{a} \mathrm{b} \mathrm{c}] = (z\hat{i} - 3\hat{j} + \hat{k}) \cdot (x\hat{i} + y\hat{j} + z\hat{k})$.

Substitute the values $x=1, y=1, z=6$:
$[\mathrm{a} \mathrm{b} \mathrm{c}] = (6\hat{i} - 3\hat{j} + \hat{k}) \cdot (1\hat{i} + 1\hat{j} + 6\hat{k})$.

$[\mathrm{a} \mathrm{b} \mathrm{c}] = (6 \times 1) + (-3 \times 1) + (1 \times 6) = 6 - 3 + 6 = 9$.

Answer: 9

$E_\min = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda_\max} = \dfrac{1240\,\text{eV·nm}}{700\,\text{nm}} \approx 1.77\,\text{eV} \approx 1.8\,\text{eV}$

Correct option: (3)

(A) ${FeSO}_{4} + {\left({NH}_{4}\right)}_{2}{SO}_{4} + 6{H}_{2}O \to {FeSO}_{4} \cdot {\left({NH}_{4}\right)}_{2}{SO}_{4} \cdot 6{H}_{2}O$(Mohr's salt)

Mohr’s salt called double salt which contains more than one simple salt. It undergoes complete dissociation in aqueous solutions.

(B) ${CuSO}_{4} \cdot 4{NH}_{3} \cdot {H}_{2}O$

Ammonia solution in water gives a blue precipitate when it combines with a solution of copper salt. The pale blue precipitate of copper hydroxide dissolves in excess of ammonium hydroxide forming tetraamine copper[II] sulphate, an azure blue (deep blue) soluble complex salt.

(C) ${K}_{2}{SO}_{4} \cdot {Al}_{2}{\left({SO}_{4}\right)}_{3} \cdot 24{H}_{2}O$ (Potash alum)

It is a double salt. Basically, it is comprised of two simple salts potassium sulphate and aluminium sulphate. Potash alum will not be wet in its solid form because the water of crystallisation is not free.

(D) $Fe ( CN{)}_{2} \cdot 4KCN$

It is complex salt. It does not dissociate completely into individual ions.

So, the correct answer is A and C only.

29641.subject: Chemistry
29641.text: In sulphur estimation, $2.0 \times 10^{-3}$ mol of an organic compound (X) (molar mass $76$ g mol$^{-1}$) gave $0.4813$ g of barium sulphate (molar mass $233$ g mol$^{-1}$). The percentage of sulphur in the compound (X) is ______ $\times 10^{-1}$ % (Nearest integer)
29641.sol:
Mass of the organic compound (X) can be calculated as:

$\text{Mass of X} = \text{Moles} \times \text{Molar mass}$

$\text{Mass of X} = 2.0 \times 10^{-3} \text{ mol} \times 76 \text{ g mol}^{-1} = 0.152 \text{ g}$

In the Carius method for sulphur estimation, the mass of sulphur in the given mass of $\text{BaSO}_4$ is:

$\text{Mass of S} = \dfrac{32}{233} \times \text{Mass of BaSO}_4$

$\text{Mass of S} = \dfrac{32}{233} \times 0.4813 \text{ g} \approx 0.0661 \text{ g}$

The percentage of sulphur in the organic compound is given by:

$\text{\% of S} = \dfrac{\text{Mass of S}}{\text{Mass of X}} \times 100$

$\text{\% of S} = \dfrac{0.0661}{0.152} \times 100 \approx 43.487 \text{ \%}$

To express this in the requested format:

$43.487 \text{ \%} = 434.87 \times 10^{-1} \text{ \%}$

Rounding to the nearest integer, we get $435$.

Answer: $435$

32127.text:
Van der Waal's equation for a gas is stated as,

$\text{P} = \dfrac{\text{nRT}}{\text{V} - \text{nb}} - \text{a}{\left(\dfrac{\text{n}}{\text{V}}\right)}^{2}$.

This equation reduces to the perfect gas equation, $\text{P} = \dfrac{\text{nRT}}{\text{V}}$ When,
options: temperature is sufficiently high and pressure is low.
both temperature and pressure are very low.
both temperature and pressure are very high.
temperature is sufficiently low and pressure is high.
32127.sol:
At very high temperatures & low pressures, the characteristic constant behaviour can be understood from virial expansion

$\text{Z} = \dfrac{{\text{PV}}_{\text{m}}}{\text{RT}} = 1 + \left(\text{b} - \dfrac{\text{a}}{\text{RT}}\right) \dfrac{1}{{\text{V}}_{\text{m}}} + \dfrac{{\text{b}}^{2}}{{\text{V}}_{\text{m}}^{2}} + \text{....}$

${V}_{m}$, molar volume large i.e $\dfrac{{\text{b}}^{2}}{{\text{V}}_{\text{m}}^{2}} \to \text{o}$

i.e Third term in virial expansion can be ignored.

In qualitative terms, the real gas will show ideal behaviour when the intermolecular forces of attraction will be negligible which is possible at high temperature and low pressure.
Also $\left(\text{b} - \dfrac{\text{a}}{\text{RT}}\right) \to \text{o}$

i.e. $\text{Z} \approx 1$ and gas behaves ideally.

32994.text:
Let $f(x)$ be a polynomial of degree 4 having extreme values at $x=1$ and $x=2$.
If $\lim _{x \rightarrow 0}\left(\frac{f(x)}{x^2}+1\right)=3$ then $f(-1)$ is equal to
32994.sol:
$\because f(x)$ has extremum values at x=1 and $x=2\because f^{\prime}(1)=0 and f^{\prime}(2)=0$
As, $f(x)$ is a polynomial of degree 4 .
Suppose $f(x)=A x^4+B x^3+C x^2+D x+E \begin{aligned}$&\because $\lim _{x \rightarrow 0}\left(\frac{f(x)}{x^2}+$1\right)=3 \\
&\Rightarrow $\lim _{x \rightarrow 0}\left(\frac{A x^4+B x^3+C x^2+D x+E}{x^2}+$1\right)=3 \\
&\Rightarrow $\lim _{x \rightarrow 0}\left(A x²+B x+C+\frac{D}{x}+\frac{E}{x^2}$+$1\right)=3
\end{aligned}

As limit has finite value, so $D=0 and E=0$
Now A(0)^2+B(0)+C+0+0+1=3 \begin{aligned}$&\Rightarrow c+1=3 \Rightarrow c=2 \\
&f^{\prime}(x)=4 A x³+3 B x²+2 C x+D \\
&f^{\prime}(1)=0 \Rightarrow 4 A(1)+3 B(1)+2 C(1)+D=0
\end{aligned}

$\begin{aligned}$& \Rightarrow 4 A+3 B=-4 \\
f^{\prime}(2)=0 & \Rightarrow 4 A(8)+3 B(4)+2 C(2)+D=0 \\
& \Rightarrow 8 A+3 B=-2
\end{aligned} From $equations (1) and (2), we getA=\frac{1}{2} and B=-2$
So, $f(x)=\frac{x^4}{2}-2 x^3+2 x^2$
Therefore, $f(-1)=\frac{(-1)^4}{2}-2(-1)^3+2(-1)^2$
=$\frac{1}{2}+$2+2=$\frac{9}{2}Hence $f(-1)=$\frac{9}{2}$

33891.subject: Mathematics
33891.text: If $\left(\dfrac{1 + i}{1 - i}\right)\dfrac{m}{2} = \left(\dfrac{1 + i}{i - 1}\right)\dfrac{n}{3} = 1, \left(m, n \in N\right)$ then the greatest common divisor of the least values of $m$ and $n$ is
33891.sol:
$\left(\dfrac{1 + i}{1 - i}\right)\dfrac{m}{2} = \left(\dfrac{1 + i}{i - 1}\right)\dfrac{n}{3} = 1$

Rationalize both the terms

$\left(\dfrac{1 + i}{1 - i} \times \dfrac{1 + i}{1 + i}\right)\dfrac{m}{2} = \left(\dfrac{1 + i}{i - 1} \times \dfrac{- 1 - i}{- 1 - i}\right)\dfrac{n}{3} = 1$

$\left(\dfrac{1 + {i}^{2} + 2i}{1 - {i}^{2}}\right)\dfrac{m}{2} = \left(\dfrac{- 1 - {i}^{2} - 2i}{{\left(- 1\right)}^{2} - {i}^{2}}\right)\dfrac{n}{3} = 1$

We know ${i}^{2} = - 1$

$\left(\dfrac{2i}{2}\right)\dfrac{m}{2} = \left(\dfrac{- 2i}{2}\right)\dfrac{n}{3} = 1$

$\left(i\right)\dfrac{m}{2} = \left(- i\right)\dfrac{n}{3} = 1$

For $\left(i\right)\dfrac{m}{2} = 1 ⇒ \dfrac{m}{2} = 4k ⇒ m = 8k, k \in I$

Since $m$ is natural number so the least value of $m$ is $8$.

For $\left(- i\right)\dfrac{n}{3} = 1 ⇒ \dfrac{n}{3} = 4l ⇒ n = 12l, l \in I$

Since $n$ is natural number so the least value of $n$ is $12$.

So greatest common factor of $8 and 12$ is $4$.

34190.text: Let $f, g: \left(0, \infty\right) \to R$ be two functions defined by $f\left(x\right) = {∫}_{- x}^{x}\left(\left|t\right| - {t}^{2}\right){e}^{- {t}^{2}}dt$ and $g\left(x\right) = {∫}_{0}^{{x}^{2}}t\dfrac{1}{2}{e}^{- {t}^{2}}dt$. Then the value of $9\left(f\left(\sqrt{{\log}_{e}9} + g\left(\sqrt{{\log}_{e}9}\right\right)\right)$ is equal to
34190.sol:
Given: $g\left(x\right) = {∫}_{0}^{{x}^{2}}t\dfrac{1}{2}{e}^{- t}dt$

Let, $t = {y}^{2}$

$⇒ dt = 2ydy$

$⇒ g\left(x\right) = {∫}_{0}^{x}2{y}^{2}{e}^{- {y}^{2}}dy$

$⇒ g\left(x\right) = 2{∫}_{0}^{x}{t}^{2}{e}^{- {t}^{2}}dt$

Also, $f\left(x\right) = 2{∫}_{0}^{x}\left(t - {t}^{2}\right){e}^{- {t}^{2}}dt$y

$⇒ f\left(x\right) + g\left(x\right) = 2{∫}_{0}^{x}t{e}^{- {t}^{2}}dt$

Let, ${t}^{2} = p$

$⇒ 2tdt = dp$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) + g\left(x\right) = {∫}_{0}^{{x}^{2}}{e}^{- p}dp$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) + g\left(x\right) = 1 - {e}^{- {x}^{2}}$

$⇒ 9f\left(\sqrt{{\log}_{e}9}\right) + g\left(\sqrt{{\log}_{e}9}\right) = 9\left(1 - {e}^{- log9}\right)$

$⇒ 9f\left(\sqrt{{\log}_{e}9}\right) + g\left(\sqrt{{\log}_{e}9}\right) = 9\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{9}\right)$

$⇒ 9f\left(\sqrt{{\log}_{e}9}\right) + g\left(\sqrt{{\log}_{e}9}\right) = 8$

34282.text: Let $\mathop{Max}_{0 ⩽ x ⩽ 2}\left\{\dfrac{9 - {x}^{2}}{5 - x}\right\} = \alpha$ and $\mathop{Min}_{0 ⩽ x ⩽ 2}\left\{\dfrac{9 - {x}^{2}}{5 - x}\right\} = \beta$. If ${∫}_{\beta - \dfrac{8}{3}}^{2\alpha - 1} Max \left\{\dfrac{9 - {x}^{2}}{5 - x}, x\right\}dx = {\alpha}_{1} + {\alpha}_{2}{\log}_{e}\left(\dfrac{8}{15}\right)$, then ${\alpha}_{1} + {\alpha}_{2}$ is equal to ______
34282.sol:
Here $y = \dfrac{9 - {x}^{2}}{5 - x} = 5 + x + \dfrac{16}{x - 5}$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 1 - \dfrac{16}{{\left(x - 5\right)}^{2}}$

When $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0 ⇒ 1 - \dfrac{16}{{\left(x - 5\right)}^{2}} = 0$

34736.text: The differential equation of the family of circles passing through the points $\left(0, 2\right)$ and $\left(0, - 2\right)$ is
34736.sol:
Given a circle passing through $\left(0, - 2\right)$ and $\left(0, 2\right)$, so its equation will be,

$\left(x - {x}_{1}\right)\left(x - {x}_{2}\right) + \left(y - {y}_{1}\right)\left(y - {y}_{2}\right) + {\lambda}_{1}\left|\begin{cases}x & y & 1 \\ {x}_{1} & {y}_{1} & 1 \\ {x}_{2} & {y}_{2} & 1\end{cases}\right| = 0, \left({\lambda}_{1} \in R\right)$

On putting the given values we get,

$⇒ \left(x - 0\right)\left(x - 0\right) + \left(y - 2\right)\left(y + 2\right) + {\lambda}_{1}\left|\begin{cases}x & y & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & - 2 & 1\end{cases}\right| = 0, \left({\lambda}_{1} \in R\right)$

$⇒ {x}^{2} + \left({y}^{2} - 4\right) + {\lambda}_{1}\left(4x\right) = 0$

$⇒ {x}^{2} + \left({y}^{2} - 4\right) + \lambdax = 0, \left(\lambda \in R\right)$

Now dividing both side by $x$ we get,

$⇒ \dfrac{{x}^{2} + \left({y}^{2} - 4\right)}{x} + \lambda = 0$

Now differentiating with respect to $x$

$⇒ \dfrac{x\left[2x + 2y \cdot \dfrac{dy}{dx}\right] - \left[{x}^{2} + {y}^{2} - 4\right] \cdot 1}{{x}^{2}} = 0$

$⇒ 2xy \cdot \dfrac{dy}{dx} + \left({x}^{2} - {y}^{2} + 4\right) = 0$

35093.subject: Mathematics
35093.text: Let $f$ be a polynomial function such that $\log_2(f(x)) = \left(\log_2\left(2+\dfrac{2}{3}+\dfrac{2}{9}+\ldots\infty\right)\right)\cdot\log_3\left(1+\dfrac{f(x)}{f(1/x)}\right)$, $x>0$ and $f(6)=37$. Then $\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^{10}f(n)$ is equal to ________.
35093.sol:
The sum of the infinite geometric progression is given by:

$S = 2 + \dfrac{2}{3} + \dfrac{2}{9} + \ldots \infty = \dfrac{2}{1 - \dfrac{1}{3}} = 3$

Substituting this into the given equation:

$\log_2(f(x)) = \log_2(3) \cdot \log_3\left(1 + \dfrac{f(x)}{f(1/x)}\right)$

Using the base change property $\log_a(b) \cdot \log_b(c) = \log_a(c)$:

$\log_2(f(x)) = \log_2\left(1 + \dfrac{f(x)}{f(1/x)}\right)$

Equating the arguments:

$f(x) = 1 + \dfrac{f(x)}{f(1/x)}$

$f(x)f(1/x) - f(1/x) = f(x)$

$f(x)f(1/x) = f(x) + f(1/x)$

The only polynomial functions satisfying this relation are of the form $f(x) = 1 \pm x^n$.

Given $f(6) = 37$:

$1 \pm 6^n = 37$

Taking the positive sign, $6^n = 36 \Rightarrow n = 2$.

Thus, the polynomial is $f(x) = x^2 + 1$.

The required sum is:

$\sum_{n=1}^{10} f(n) = \sum_{n=1}^{10} (n^2 + 1)$

$\sum_{n=1}^{10} f(n) = \sum_{n=1}^{10} n^2 + \sum_{n=1}^{10} 1$

$\sum_{n=1}^{10} f(n) = \dfrac{10 \times 11 \times 21}{6} + 10$

$\sum_{n=1}^{10} f(n) = 385 + 10 = 395$

Answer: $395$

35094.text: Let $f: \mathbb{R} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ be defined as $f(x) = \dfrac{2x^2 - 3x + 2}{3x^2 + x + 3}$. Then $f$ is :
35094.sol:
Given $f(x) = \dfrac{2x^2 - 3x + 2}{3x^2 + x + 3}$

To check for one-one, let $f(x) = f(y)$

$\dfrac{2x^2 - 3x + 2}{3x^2 + x + 3} = \dfrac{2y^2 - 3y + 2}{3y^2 + y + 3}$

Cross-multiplying and simplifying, we get:

$11x^2y - 11xy^2 - 11x + 11y = 0$

$11xy(x - y) - 11(x - y) = 0$

$11(x - y)(xy - 1) = 0$

This implies $x = y$ or $xy = 1$.

Since $f(x) = f(1/x)$ for $x \neq 0$ (for example, $f(2) = f(1/2) = \dfrac{4}{17}$), the function is many-one (not one-one).

To check for onto, let $y = \dfrac{2x^2 - 3x + 2}{3x^2 + x + 3}$

$(3y - 2)x^2 + (y + 3)x + (3y - 2) = 0$

For $x \in \mathbb{R}$, the discriminant $D \ge 0$:

$(y + 3)^2 - 4(3y - 2)^2 \ge 0$

$(y + 3 - 6y + 4)(y + 3 + 6y - 4) \ge 0$

$(7 - 5y)(7y - 1) \ge 0$

$(5y - 7)(7y - 1) \le 0$

$y \in \left[\dfrac{1}{7}, \dfrac{7}{5}\right]$

Since the range is a proper subset of the codomain $\mathbb{R}$, the function is not onto.

Thus, $f$ is neither one-one nor onto.

Answer: neither one-one nor onto

38459.sol:

Since $\vec{p} = \overrightarrow{BC}$, $\vec{q} = \overrightarrow{CA}$, and $\vec{r} = \overrightarrow{BA}$, from triangle closure $\vec{r} = \vec{p} + \vec{q}$.
$\vec{p} \cdot \vec{q} = |\vec{p}||\vec{q}|\cos\theta = 2\sqrt{3} \cdot 2 \cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} = 4$
$|\vec{r}|^2 = |\vec{p}|^2 + |\vec{q}|^2 + 2\vec{p} \cdot \vec{q} = 12 + 4 + 8 = 24$
$\vec{q} - 3\vec{r} = \vec{q} - 3(\vec{p} + \vec{q}) = -3\vec{p} - 2\vec{q}$
$\vec{p} \times (\vec{q} - 3\vec{r}) = -2(\vec{p} \times \vec{q})$
$\sin^2\theta = 1 - \frac{1}{3} = \frac{2}{3}$
$|\vec{p} \times \vec{q}|^2 = 12 \cdot 4 \cdot \frac{2}{3} = 32$
$|\vec{p} \times (\vec{q} - 3\vec{r})|^2 = 4 \cdot 32 = 128$
Result: $128 + 3(24) = 128 + 72 = 200$

39507.subject: Physics
39507.text: Two cells of emfs $1$ V and $2$ V and internal resistance $2\,\Omega$ and $1\,\Omega$, respectively connected in parallel, gave a current of $1$ A through an external resistance. If the polarity of one cell is reversed, then value of current through the external resistance will be $\dfrac{\alpha}{5}$ A. The value of $\alpha$ is __________.
39507.sol:
For two cells connected in parallel with the same polarity, the equivalent emf $E_{eq}$ and equivalent internal resistance $r_{eq}$ are given by:

$E_{eq} = \dfrac{E_1 r_2 + E_2 r_1}{r_1 + r_2}$

$r_{eq} = \dfrac{r_1 r_2}{r_1 + r_2}$

Substituting the given values ($E_1 = 1$ V, $r_1 = 2\,\Omega$, $E_2 = 2$ V, $r_2 = 1\,\Omega$):

$E_{eq} = \dfrac{1 \times 1 + 2 \times 2}{2 + 1} = \dfrac{5}{3}$ V

$r_{eq} = \dfrac{2 \times 1}{2 + 1} = \dfrac{2}{3}\,\Omega$

The current $I$ through the external resistance $R$ is $1$ A:

$I = \dfrac{E_{eq}}{R + r_{eq}}$

$1 = \dfrac{\dfrac{5}{3}}{R + \dfrac{2}{3}}$

$R + \dfrac{2}{3} = \dfrac{5}{3} \Rightarrow R = 1\,\Omega$

When the polarity of one cell is reversed, the new equivalent emf $E'_{eq}$ becomes:

$E'_{eq} = \dfrac{|E_1 r_2 - E_2 r_1|}{r_1 + r_2} = \dfrac{|1 \times 1 - 2 \times 2|}{3} = \dfrac{3}{3} = 1$ V

The equivalent internal resistance remains the same, $r_{eq} = \dfrac{2}{3}\,\Omega$.

The new current $I'$ through the external resistance $R$ is:

$I' = \dfrac{E'_{eq}}{R + r_{eq}} = \dfrac{1}{1 + \dfrac{2}{3}} = \dfrac{1}{\dfrac{5}{3}} = \dfrac{3}{5}$ A

Given that the new current is $\dfrac{\alpha}{5}$ A, we have:

$\dfrac{\alpha}{5} = \dfrac{3}{5} \Rightarrow \alpha = 3$

Answer: $3$

41889.subject: Physics
41889.text: A soap bubble of surface tension $0.04 \mathrm{~N} / \mathrm{m}$ is blown to a diameter of 7 cm. If $(15000-x) \mu \mathrm{J}$ of work is done in blowing it further to make its diameter 14 cm, then the value of $x$ is $\_\_\_\_$. ($\pi=22 / 7$)
41889.sol:
Soap bubble has two surfaces. Work done: $W = \Delta A \times \sigma$
Initial radius: $r_i = 3.5$ cm = 0.035 m, Final radius: $r_f = 7$ cm = 0.07 m
Change in surface area (both surfaces): $\Delta A = 8\pi(r_f^2 - r_i^2) = 8\pi(0.07^2 - 0.035^2)$
$\Delta A = 8\pi(0.0049 - 0.001225) = 8\pi \times 0.003675 = 0.0294\pi$ m²
$W = 0.0294\pi \times 0.04 = 0.001176\pi$ J = $0.001176 \times \frac{22}{7} = 0.003696$ J = 3696 μJ
Therefore: $x = 15000 - 3696 = 11304$

42227.text: A particle starts from origin at $t = 0$ with a velocity $5\overset{^}{i}m{s}^{- 1}$ and moves in $x - y$ plane under action of a force which produces a constant acceleration of $( 3\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} ) m{s}^{- 2}$. If the $x$-coordinate of the particle at that instant is $84m$, then the speed of the particle at this time is $\sqrt{\alpha}m{s}^{- 1}$. The value of $\alpha$ is _______.
42227.sol:
Given, ${u}_{x} = 5m{s}^{- 1}, {a}_{x} = 3m{s}^{- 2}, x = 84m$

The formula to calculate the velocity of the particle along x-axis is given by

${v}_{x}^{2} = {u}_{x}^{2} + 2ax . . . \left(1\right)$

From equation (1), it follows that

${v}_{x}^{2} = 25 + 2 ( 3 ) ( 84 ) ⇒ {v}_{x} = 23m{s}^{- 1}$

Also, the velocity of the particle along x-axis can be written as

${v}_{x} = {u}_{x} + {a}_{x}t . . . \left(2\right)$

From equation (2), it follows that

$\begin{cases}t & = & \dfrac{23 - 5}{3} \\ & = & 6s\end{cases}$

Similarly, for the $y -$ component of the velocity, it follows that

$\begin{cases}{v}_{y} & = & 0 + {a}_{y}t \\ & = & 0 + 2 \times ( 6 ) \\ & = & 12m{s}^{- 1}\end{cases}$

Hence, the magnitude of the velocity is given by

${v}^{2} = {v}_{x}^{2} + {v}_{y}^{2} = {23}^{2} + {12}^{2} = 673v = \sqrt{673}m{s}^{- 1}$

Therefore, $\alpha = 673$.

43247.text:
A solid cylinder length is suspended symmetrically through two massless strings, as shown in the figure. The distance from the initial rest position, the cylinder should be unbinding the strings to achieve a speed of $4m{s}^{- 1}$, is _____$cm$.

(take $g = 10m{s}^{- 2}$)
43247.sol:
The portion of the strings between the ceiling and the cylinder are at rest. Hence, the points of the cylinder where the strings leave it are at rest. The cylinder is thus rolling without slipping on the strings.

Now, from energy conservation

$mgh = \dfrac{1}{2}m{v}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}I{\omega}^{2}$

where, $I$ is moment of inertia of cylinder and $\omega = \dfrac{v}{R}$ is angular velocity.

Then, we have

$mgh = \dfrac{1}{2}m{v}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{m{R}^{2}}{2}{\omega}^{2} ⇒ gh = \dfrac{1}{2}{v}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{{R}^{2}}{2}{\left(\dfrac{v}{R}\right)}^{2}$

$10h = \dfrac{16}{2} + \dfrac{16}{4} ⇒ h = 1 . 2m = 120cm$

The formula to calculate the fundamental frequency in a closed pipe is given by

And, that in an open pipe is given by

Given that

$\dfrac{v}{4 \times 150} - \dfrac{v}{2 \times 350} = 7 ⇒ \dfrac{v}{600cm} - \dfrac{v}{700cm} = 7 ⇒ \dfrac{v}{6m} - \dfrac{v}{7m} = 7 ⇒ v\left(\dfrac{1}{42}\right) = 7 ⇒ v = 42 \times 7 = 294m{s}^{- 1}$

49878.subject: Physics
49878.text: In a conducting region, $10^{19}$ electrons and $10^{19}$ protons move to the left, while $10^{19}\alpha$-particles move to the right per second. The resulting electric current is $(e = 1.6 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C})$ _________
49878.sol:
The electric current is given by the rate of flow of positive charge. The direction of current is the direction of flow of positive charge, and opposite to the direction of flow of negative charge.

Current due to electrons moving left:
$I_e = n_e e = 10^{19} \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19} = 1.6$ A towards right.

Current due to protons moving left:
$I_p = n_p e = 10^{19} \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19} = 1.6$ A towards left.

Current due to $\alpha$-particles moving right:
$I_{\alpha} = n_{\alpha} (2e) = 10^{19} \times 2 \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19} = 3.2$ A towards right.

Taking the rightward direction as positive, the net current is:
$I_{net} = I_e - I_p + I_{\alpha}$

$I_{net} = 1.6 - 1.6 + 3.2 = 3.2$ A

The resulting electric current is $3.2$ A towards right.

Answer: $3.2$ A towards right

53854.text: 10 different toys are to be distributed among 10 children. Total number of ways of distributing these toys, so that exactly two children do not get any toy, is
53854.sol:
There may be two cases.
Case I. Two children get none and one get three and others get one each.
Then, total number. of ways $=\frac{10!}{2!\times 3!\times 7!} \times 10!$
Case II. Two get none and two get 2 each and the others get one each.
Then, total number of ways $=\frac{10!}{(2!)^4 \times 6!} \times 10!$
Hence, total number of ways
$=\frac{(10!)^2}{2!\times 3!\times 7!}+\frac{(10!)^2}{(2!)^4 \times 6!}=\frac{(10!)^2 \times 25}{(2!)^2 \times 6!\times 84}$

55289.subject: Chemistry
55289.text: Which from following reaction results in azo coupling?
55289.sol:
Azo coupling is an electrophilic aromatic substitution reaction involving an arenediazonium salt and an electron-rich aromatic compound like phenol or aniline, forming an azo compound with the $\mathrm{-N=N-}$ linkage, often used as dyes.

A: Aniline reacts with nitrous acid to form benzenediazonium chloride ($\mathrm{C_6H_5N_2^+Cl^-}$). This is diazotization, producing a precursor, not azo coupling: $\mathrm{C_6H_5NH_2 + HNO_2 + HCl \xrightarrow{0-5^{{}^{\circ}}\mathrm{C}} C_6H_5N_2^+Cl^- + 2H_2O}$.

B: Benzenediazonium chloride reacts with phenol in alkaline medium, coupling at the para-position due to the activating hydroxyl group: $\mathrm{C_6H_5N_2^+Cl^- + C_6H_5OH \xrightarrow{OH^-} C_6H_5-N=N-C_6H_4-OH\ (p) + HCl}$. This is a classic azo coupling.

C: Benzenediazonium chloride reacts with $\mathrm{HBF_4}$ to form diazonium fluoroborate, an intermediate in the Balz-Schieman reaction for fluorobenzene synthesis, not azo coupling: $\mathrm{C_6H_5N_2^+Cl^- + HBF_4 \rightarrow C_6H_5N_2^+BF_4^- + HCl}$.

D: Benzenediazonium chloride undergoes substitution with copper powder and HCl to form chlorobenzene, known as the Gattermann reaction, not azo coupling: $\mathrm{C_6H_5N_2^+Cl^- \xrightarrow[\mathrm{HCl}]{Cu\ (Powder)} C_6H_5Cl + N_2}$.

Thus, only option B represents an azo coupling reaction.

55796.subject: Chemistry
55796.sol:
Using VSEPR theory, the shape of $\mathrm{BrF}_5$ is determined by its electron and molecular geometries.
Bromine contributes 7 valence electrons, and each fluorine contributes 7, for a total of $1 \times 7 + 5 \times 7 = 42$ valence electrons.

Five single bonds use $5 \times 2 = 10$ electrons.
The remaining $42 - 10 = 32$ electrons are allocated as lone pairs.
Each fluorine requires 6 electrons to complete its octet, using $5 \times 6 = 30$ electrons.
The final $32 - 30 = 2$ electrons form one lone pair on bromine.

Thus, bromine has 5 bonding pairs and 1 lone pair, for a steric number of $5 + 1 = 6$.

An octahedral electron geometry with one lone pair yields a square pyramidal molecular geometry.

Final answer: The shape is square pyramidal, corresponding to choice $\boxed{C}$.

55987.subject: Chemistry
55987.text: Which of the following is an example of second order reaction ?
55987.sol:
The order of a reaction is determined experimentally by its rate law.

For the decomposition of hydrogen peroxide, the rate law is Rate = $k[\text{H}_2\text{O}_2]$. It is a first-order reaction.

For the thermal decomposition of acetaldehyde, the rate law is Rate = $k[\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}]^{1.5}$. It is a fractional-order (1.5) reaction.

For the reaction between $\text{NO}_2$ and $\text{F}_2$, the mechanism involves a slow rate-determining step: $\text{NO}_2 + \text{F}_2 \rightarrow \text{NO}_2\text{F} + \text{F}$. The rate law is Rate = $k[\text{NO}_2][\text{F}_2]$. The overall order is $1 + 1 = 2$, making it a second-order reaction.

For the reaction between $\text{NO}$ and $\text{H}_2$, the rate law is Rate = $k[\text{NO}]^2[\text{H}_2]$. The overall order is $2 + 1 = 3$, making it a third-order reaction.

Thus, $2\,\text{NO}_{2(g)} + \text{F}_{2(g)} \rightarrow 2\text{NO}_2\text{F}_{(g)}$ is the correct example of a second-order reaction.

Answer: $2\,\text{NO}_{2(g)} + \text{F}_{2(g)} \rightarrow 2\text{NO}_2\text{F}_{(g)}$

55994.subject: Chemistry
55994.text: If for a first-order reaction, $[A]_0 = 1.0\ \text{M}$ and $[A]_t = 0.25\ \text{M}$ after 276 s, find the value of the rate constant (k).
55994.sol:
For a first-order reaction, the concentration after $n$ half-lives is given by $[A]_t = \dfrac{[A]_0}{2^n}$.

Given $[A]_0 = 1.0\ \text{M}$ and $[A]_t = 0.25\ \text{M}$, we have:

$0.25 = \dfrac{1.0}{2^n} \Rightarrow 2^n = 4 \Rightarrow n = 2$

Thus, two half-lives have passed in $276\ \text{s}$.

$2 t_{1/2} = 276\ \text{s} \Rightarrow t_{1/2} = 138\ \text{s}$

The rate constant $k$ is given by:

$k = \dfrac{0.693}{t_{1/2}} = \dfrac{0.693}{138}$

$k \approx 0.0050\ \texts^{-1}$

59866.text:
Calculate the work done for the following reaction at $27\,^\circ\text{C}$

59866.sol:
The given reaction is $\text{C}_2\text{H}_{4(g)} + \text{H}_{2(g)} \longrightarrow \text{C}_2\text{H}_{6(g)}$

Change in number of moles of gaseous species, $\Delta n_g = n_p - n_r$

$\Delta n_g = 1 - (1 + 1) = -1$

Work done, $W = -\Delta n_g RT$

$W = -(-1) \times 8.314 \times (27 + 273)$

$W = 1 \times 8.314 \times 300$

$W = 2494.2$ J

Answer: $2494.2$ J

62741.subject: Mathematics
62741.sol:
Evaluating $\lim_{x \to 3} \frac{(84-x)^{\frac{1}{4}}-3}{x-3}$ by substitution gives the indeterminate form $\frac{0}{0}$, so we apply L'Hôpital's Rule.

Differentiating numerator and denominator:

$f(x) = (84-x)^{\frac{1}{4}}-3$
$f'(x) = -\frac{1}{4}(84-x)^{-\frac{3}{4}}$

$g(x) = x-3$
$g'(x) = 1$

The limit becomes:

$\lim_{x \to 3} \frac{-\frac{1}{4}(84-x)^{-\frac{3}{4}}}{1} = -\frac{1}{4}(81)^{-\frac{3}{4}}$

Simplifying through exponent rules:

$-\frac{1}{4}(3^4)^{-\frac{3}{4}} = -\frac{1}{4} \cdot 3^{-3} = -\frac{1}{4} \cdot \frac{1}{27} = -\frac{1}{108}$

Final answer: $\boxed{-\frac{1}{108}}$

62810.subject: Mathematics
62810.text: The LPP maximize $z = 2x + 5y$ subject to $x + 3y \leq 6$, $2x + 6y \leq 18$, $x \geq 0$, $y \geq 0$ has
62810.sol:
The given constraints are:
$x + 3y \leq 6$
$2x + 6y \leq 18 \Rightarrow x + 3y \leq 9$
$x \geq 0, y \geq 0$

The second constraint $x + 3y \leq 9$ is redundant since $x + 3y \leq 6$ is a stricter condition. The feasible region is bounded by $x + 3y \leq 6$ in the first quadrant, which forms a triangle.

The vertices of the feasible region are $(0,0)$, $(6,0)$, and $(0,2)$.

Evaluating the objective function $z = 2x + 5y$ at these vertices:
At $(0,0)$, $z = 2(0) + 5(0) = 0$
At $(6,0)$, $z = 2(6) + 5(0) = 12$
At $(0,2)$, $z = 2(0) + 5(2) = 10$

The maximum value of $z$ is $12$, which occurs exactly at one vertex $(6,0)$.

Therefore, the LPP has a unique solution.

Answer: Unique solution

63119.subject: Mathematics
63119.text: Which of the following statement is contingency?
63119.sol:
Key Idea : A statement which is neither a tautology nor a contradiction is a contingency.
Option (1) $\left(p ∨ q\right)$∨ ∼ q$
$≡ p ∨ $\left(q ∨ ∼ q\right)$≡ p ∨ T$
$≡$ T which is a tautology.
Option (2) \left(p ∨ q\right) ∨ ∼$
$≡ \left(p ∨ q\right) ∨ ∼$
$≡ \left(p ∨ ∼ q\right) ∨ q ≡ T ∨ q$
$≡$ T which is tautology
Option (3) $\left(p ∨ q\right)$∧ ∼ q$
$≡ $\left(p ∧ ∼ q\right)$∨ $\left(q ∧ ∼ q\right)$≡ $\left(p ∧ ∼ q\right)$∨ F$
$≡ $\left(p ∧ ∼ q\right)$
If $p \to T, q \to T$
Then $p ∧ ∼ q \to F$
If $p \to T, q \to F$
Then $p ∧ ∼ q \to T$
So, $\left(p ∧ ∼ q\right)$ is a contingency.
Therefore statement $\left(p ∨ q\right)$∧ ∼ q$ is contingency.$

63335.text: To convert the equation $2 x^2+4 x y+5 y^2-4 x-22 y+29=0$ to homogeneous form the origin is shifted to the point
63335.sol:
The general second-degree equation is given as $ax^2 + 2hxy + by^2 + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0$. Comparing with $2x^2 + 4xy + 5y^2 - 4x - 22y + 29 = 0$ yields:

$a = 2$, $h = 2$, $b = 5$, $g = -2$, $f = -11$, and $c = 29$.

The center $(x_0, y_0)$ satisfies:

$2x_0 + 2y_0 - 2 = 0$ and $2x_0 + 5y_0 - 11 = 0$.

Solving, $x_0 = -2$ and $y_0 = 3$.

Shifting origin to $(-2,3)$, the linear terms vanish and the constant becomes:

$c' = gx_0 + fy_0 + c = (-2)(-2) + (-11)(3) + 29 = 4 - 33 + 29 = 0$.

Thus, the homogeneous form is:

$2X^2 + 4XY + 5Y^2 = 0$.

Final Answer: B

& =\left(\frac{-2 \mathrm{ h}}{\mathrm{n}}\right)^2-\frac{4 \mathrm{ m}}{\mathrm{n}}=\frac{4 \mathrm{ h}^2-4 \mathrm{mn}}{\mathrm{n}^2}=\frac{3 \mathrm{ m}^2+6 \mathrm{mn}+3 \mathrm{n}^2}{\mathrm{n}^2} \ldots[\text{ From (1)] }\\
& =\frac{3(\mathrm{ m}+\mathrm{n})^2}{\mathrm{n}^2}\\
& \therefore \mathrm{m}_{1}- \mathrm{m}_{2}=\frac{\sqrt{3}(\mathrm{ m}+\mathrm{n})}{\mathrm{n}}
\end{aligned}\therefore$ Let $\theta$ be the required angle. $\begin{aligned}& \text{ Now } \tan \theta=\frac{\left|\mathrm{m}_1-\mathrm{m}_2\right|}{1+\mathrm{m}_1 \mathrm{ m}_2}\\
& =\frac{\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}(\mathrm{ m}+\mathrm{n})}{\mathrm{n}}\right)}{\left(1+\frac{\mathrm{m}}{\mathrm{n}}\right)}=\frac{\sqrt{3}(\mathrm{ m}+\mathrm{n})}{\mathrm{n}} \times \frac{\mathrm{n}}{\mathrm{m}+\mathrm{n}}=\sqrt{3} \Rightarrow \theta=60^{{}^{\circ}}=\frac{\pi^{\mathrm{c}}}{3}
\end{aligned}$

64819.text: The number of common solutions of the pair of equations $2\sin^2\theta - 2\cos^2\theta + 1 = 0$ and $2\sin^2\theta + 3\sin\theta - 2 = 0$ in the interval $[0, 2\pi]$, is
64819.sol:
Given the second equation:

$2\sin^2\theta + 3\sin\theta - 2 = 0$

$(2\sin\theta - 1)(\sin\theta + 2) = 0$

Since $\sin\theta \in [-1,1]$, $\sin\theta = -2$ is rejected. Thus, $\sin\theta = \dfrac{1}{2}$.

Given the first equation:

$2\sin^2\theta - 2\cos^2\theta + 1 = 0$

$2\sin^2\theta - 2(1 - \sin^2\theta) + 1 = 0$

$4\sin^2\theta - 1 = 0$

$\sin^2\theta = \dfrac{1}{4} \Rightarrow \sin\theta = \pm \dfrac{1}{2}$

The common solution for both equations is $\sin\theta = \dfrac{1}{2}$.

In the interval $[0, 2\pi]$, the solutions for $\sin\theta = \dfrac{1}{2}$ are $\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$ and $\theta = \dfrac{5\pi}{6}$.

Therefore, the number of common solutions is $2$.

Answer: $2$

65120.text: If a parallelogram is constructed on the vectors $\bar{a} = 3\bar{p} - \bar{q}, \bar{b} = \bar{p} + 3\bar{q}$ and $|\bar{p}| = 3, |\bar{q}| = 2$ and angle between $\bar{p}$ and $\bar{q}$ is $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$, then the ratio of the lengths of adjacent sides $\bar{a}$ and $\bar{b}$ of the parallelogram is
65120.sol:
Given $\bar{a} = 3\bar{p} - \bar{q}$ and $\bar{b} = \bar{p} + 3\bar{q}$.

We are given $|\bar{p}| = 3$, $|\bar{q}| = 2$, and the angle between $\bar{p}$ and $\bar{q}$ is $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$.

The dot product of $\bar{p}$ and $\bar{q}$ is:

$\bar{p} \cdot \bar{q} = |\bar{p}| |\bar{q}| \cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = 3 \times 2 \times \dfrac{1}{2} = 3$

The length of side $\bar{a}$ is given by:

$|\bar{a}|^2 = |3\bar{p} - \bar{q}|^2 = 9|\bar{p}|^2 + |\bar{q}|^2 - 6(\bar{p} \cdot \bar{q})$

$|\bar{a}|^2 = 9(3)^2 + (2)^2 - 6(3) = 81 + 4 - 18 = 67$

$\Rightarrow |\bar{a}| = \sqrt{67}$

The length of side $\bar{b}$ is given by:

$|\bar{b}|^2 = |\bar{p} + 3\bar{q}|^2 = |\bar{p}|^2 + 9|\bar{q}|^2 + 6(\bar{p} \cdot \bar{q})$

$|\bar{b}|^2 = (3)^2 + 9(2)^2 + 6(3) = 9 + 36 + 18 = 63$

$\Rightarrow |\bar{b}| = \sqrt{63}$

The ratio of the lengths of adjacent sides $\bar{a}$ and $\bar{b}$ is $|\bar{a}| : |\bar{b}| = \sqrt{67} : \sqrt{63}$.

Answer: $\sqrt{67} : \sqrt{63}$

Expanding the determinant along the first row:

$-ac - ab + ac + c^2 = 0$

$c^2 - ab = 0$

$c^2 = ab$

Since $a, b, c$ are non-negative numbers, $c = $\sqrt{ab}.

Thus, $c$ is the geometric mean of $a$ and $b$.

The volume of the parallelepiped is determined by the scalar triple product of the given vectors:

$\vec{a} = (1, 0, -1)$

$\vec{b} = (\lambda, 1, 1-\lambda)$

$\vec{c} = (\mu, \lambda, 1+\lambda-\mu)$

Evaluating the determinant:

$V = \left| \begin{vmatrix} 1 \text{ and } 0 \text{ and } -1 \\ \lambda \text{ and } 1 \text{ and } 1-\lambda \\ \mu \text{ and } \lambda \text{ and } 1+\lambda-\mu \end{vmatrix} \right|$

Expanding along the first row yields:

$V = \left| (1+\lambda-\mu - \lambda + \lambda^2) - (\lambda^2 - \mu) \right| = \left| 1 \right| = 1$

The volume simplifies to a constant value of 1, independent of both $\lambda$ and $\mu$.

Therefore, the volume depends on neither parameter.

66567.subject: Physics
66567.text: An electron of mass ' m ' and charge ' e ' initially at rest gets accelerated by a constant electric field ' $E$ '. The rate of change of de-Broglie wavelength of the electron at time ' $t$ ' is (Ignore relativistic effect) ( $\mathrm{h}=$ Planck's constant)
66567.sol:
The electron of mass $m$ and charge $e$ is initially at rest in a constant electric field $E$. The force on the electron is $F = eE$, producing acceleration $a = \frac{eE}{m}$.

With initial velocity zero, the velocity at time $t$ is $v = at = \frac{eEt}{m}$.

The de Broglie wavelength is $\lambda = \frac{h}{mv} = \frac{h}{m \cdot \frac{eEt}{m}} = \frac{h}{eEt}$.

Differentiating with respect to time gives the rate of change:

$\frac{d\lambda}{dt} = \frac{d}{dt}\left(\frac{h}{eE}t^{-1}\right) = -\frac{h}{eE}t^{-2} = -\frac{h}{eEt^2}$

This corresponds to option A.

67641.text: A particle of charge '$q$' and mass '$m$' moves in a circular orbit of radius '$r$' with angular speed '$\omega$'. The ratio of the magnitude of its magnetic moment to that of its angular momentum depends upon
67641.sol:
Magnetic moment of the revolving charge is given by $M = IA$

Current $I = \dfrac{q}{T} = \dfrac{q\omega}{2\pi}$

Area $A = \pi r^2$

$M = \left(\dfrac{q\omega}{2\pi}\right)(\pi r^2) = \dfrac{1}{2}q\omega r^2$

Angular momentum of the particle is $L = mvr = m(\omega r)r = m\omega r^2$

The ratio of the magnitude of magnetic moment to that of angular momentum is $\dfrac{M}{L} = \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{2}q\omega r^2}{m\omega r^2} = \dfrac{q}{2m}$

This ratio depends only on $q$ and $m$.

Answer: q and m

69414.text: Which of the following logic gates will have an output of '1' (one) for the given inputs?
69414.sol:
Let us evaluate the output for each logic gate given in the options:

For gate (A): It is a NAND gate with inputs $1$ and $1$.
Output $Y = \overline{1 \cdot 1} = \overline{1} = 0$

For gate (B): It is a NAND gate with inputs $1$ and $0$.
Output $Y = \overline{1 \cdot 0} = \overline{0} = 1$

For gate (C): It is a NOR gate with inputs $0$ and $1$.
Output $Y = \overline{0 + 1} = \overline{1} = 0$

For gate (D): It is an XOR gate with inputs $0$ and $0$.
Output $Y = 0 \oplus 0 = 0$

Therefore, only gate (B) has an output of $1$.

Answer: B

70179.text: In Young's double slit experiment, the distance between the slits is 2 mm and the slits are 1 m away, from the screen. Two interference patterns can be obtained on the screen due to light of wavelength ' $\lambda_1$ ' and ' $\lambda_2$ ' respectively. Position of the $n$ th order bright fringe: $y_n = \frac{n \lambda D}{d}$.

Given $\lambda_2 = 1.5\lambda_1$, the positions for $n = 3$ are:

$y_{3,1} = \frac{3\lambda_1 D}{d}$,

$y_{3,2} = \frac{3(1.5\lambda_1) D}{d} = \frac{4.5\lambda_1 D}{d}$.

The separation is

$\Delta y = y_{3,2} - y_{3,1} = \frac{(4.5 - 3)\lambda_1 D}{d} = \frac{1.5\lambda_1 D}{d}$.

Substituting $D = 1 \text{ m}$ and $d = 2 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m}$,

$\Delta y = \frac{1.5 \cdot 1}{2 \times 10^{-3}} \lambda_1 = (0.75 \times 10^{+3}) \lambda_1$.

The result corresponds to option A.

70427.subject: Physics
70427.text: The enclosed air inside a closed box of rigid walls has pressure $P_1$. The density of air inside this box is constant. On heating the gas, the pressure of the enclosed air is increased from $P_1$ to $P_2$. Now it is observed that the sound travels $1.4$ times faster than at pressure $P_1$. The ratio $P_2$ by $P_1$ is
70427.sol:
The speed of sound in a gas is given by $v = \sqrt{\dfrac{\gamma P}{\rho}}$.

Since the box has rigid walls, the volume is constant. The mass of the enclosed air is also constant, which means the density $\rho$ remains constant.

Thus, the speed of sound is directly proportional to the square root of pressure, $v \propto \sqrt{P}$.

$\dfrac{v_2}{v_1} = \sqrt{\dfrac{P_2}{P_1}}$

Given that $v_2 = 1.4 v_1$, we have:

$1.4 = \sqrt{\dfrac{P_2}{P_1}}$

Squaring both sides gives:

$\dfrac{P_2}{P_1} = (1.4)^2 = 1.96$

Answer: $1.96$

71650.subject: Chemistry
71650.text: Identify the weakest base almong the following.
71650.sol:
Phenyl amine (aniline) has a benzene ring attached to the amino group.

The lone pair of electrons on the nitrogen atom is delocalized over the benzene ring due to resonance.

This delocalization decreases the electron density on the nitrogen atom, making the lone pair less available for protonation.

In contrast, ammonia has no such delocalization, and aliphatic amines (iso-propyl amine and n-propyl amine) have electron-donating alkyl groups (+I effect) that increase the electron density on nitrogen, making them stronger bases than ammonia.

Thus, phenyl amine is the weakest base among the given options.

Answer: Phenyl amine

The sentence introduces a new, unrelated topic or an incidental piece of information into the conversation.

"For one thing" is used to introduce one of several reasons.

"In the first place" is used to introduce the first of a series of points.

"As a result" is used to indicate a consequence.

Pigments provide colour and hiding power to the paint. $\text{TiO}_2$ is a widely used white pigment. Pair I is correctly matched.

Driers accelerate the drying of the paint film by catalysing the oxidation of the drying oil. Common driers are naphthenates, resinates, and linoleates of metals like cobalt, manganese, and lead. Pair II is incorrectly matched.

Thinners are volatile solvents added to reduce the viscosity of the paint, making it easier to apply. Turpentine is a common thinner. Pair III is incorrectly matched.

Antiskinning agents are added to prevent the formation of an insoluble skin on the surface of the paint during storage. Polyhydroxy phenols are commonly used for this purpose. Pair IV is correctly matched.

Thus, exactly two pairs (I and IV) are correctly matched.

Answer: Two

73874.subject: General Ability
73874.text: Which one among the following statements is correct?
options: Pressure has magnitude as well as direction
As we go deeper in a liquid, the pressure decreases
Action and reaction forces act on the same object
Pascal and N/m^2 represent the same unit
73874.sol:
Pressure is a scalar quantity, meaning it has magnitude but no specific direction, as it acts equally in all directions at a point in a fluid.

As depth in a liquid increases, the pressure increases according to the relation $P = P_0 + \rho g h$.

According to Newton's third law of motion, action and reaction forces always act on two different objects.

The SI unit of pressure is defined as force per unit area, which is $\text{N/m}^2$. This unit is also known as Pascal (Pa). Therefore, Pascal and $\text{N/m}^2$ represent the same unit.

Answer: Pascal and N/m^2 represent the same unit

78340.subject: Mathematics
78340.text:
If $p$, $1$, $q$ are in AP and $p$, $2$, $q$ are in GP, then which of the following statements is/are correct?
I. $p$, $4$, $q$ are in HP.
II. $\dfrac{1}{p}$, $\dfrac{1}{4}$, $\dfrac{1}{q}$ are in AP.
Select the answer using the code given below.
78340.sol:
Since $p$, $1$, $q$ are in AP, we have $p + q = 2(1) = 2$.

Since $p$, $2$, $q$ are in GP, we have $pq = 2^2 = 4$.

For $p$, $4$, $q$ to be in HP, the middle term must be the harmonic mean of $p$ and $q$, which is given by $\dfrac{2pq}{p+q}$.

Substituting the values of $p+q$ and $pq$, we get $\dfrac{2(4)}{2} = 4$.

Thus, $p$, $4$, $q$ are in HP. Statement I is correct.

By the definition of harmonic progression, if $p$, $4$, $q$ are in HP, their reciprocals $\dfrac{1}{p}$, $\dfrac{1}{4}$, $\dfrac{1}{q}$ must be in AP.

Thus, Statement II is also correct.

Both statements I and II are correct.

Answer: Both I and II

79885.subject: Botany
79885.text: At what stage of the cell cycle arc histone proteins synthesized in a eukaryotic cell?
79885.sol: Cell cycle is the series of events in which cells replicate and make two new cells. Cell cycle consists of stages- $G_1, S, G_2$, and $M$ (karyokinesis). $\mathrm{G}_1$ is the stage where the cell is preparing to divide. It then moves into the $S$ phase where the cell copies all the DNA. S stands for synthesis phase of DNA. Histone proteins are also synthesised during the phase. After the DNA is copied and there's a complete extra set of all the genetic material, the cell moves into the $\mathrm{G}_2$ stage, where it organizes and condenses the genetic material, or starts to condense the genetic material, and prepares to divide.

80679.subject: Chemistry
80679.text:
Select the reagents that reduce nitriles to primary amines :
A. (i) $\text{LiAlH}_4$; (ii) $\text{H}_2\text{O}$
B. $\text{Sn} + \text{HCl}$
C. $\text{H}_2/\text{Ni}$
D. $\text{Na(Hg)}/\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}$
E. $\text{Br}_2/\text{aq. NaOH}$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
80679.sol:
Nitriles ($R-CN$) can be reduced to primary amines ($R-CH_2NH_2$) using strong reducing agents or catalytic hydrogenation.

Reagent A: $\text{LiAlH}_4$ followed by hydrolysis is a strong reducing agent that reduces nitriles to primary amines.

Reagent C: $\text{H}_2/\text{Ni}$ (catalytic hydrogenation) reduces nitriles to primary amines.

Reagent D: $\text{Na(Hg)}/\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}$ (Mendius reduction) provides nascent hydrogen and reduces nitriles to primary amines.

Reagent B: $\text{Sn} + \text{HCl}$ is typically used to reduce nitro compounds to amines. (Note: $\text{SnCl}_2 + \text{HCl}$ is used in Stephen reduction to convert nitriles to aldehydes).

Reagent E: $\text{Br}_2/\text{aq. NaOH}$ is used for Hoffmann bromamide degradation to convert amides to primary amines, not nitriles.

Thus, A, C, and D are the correct reagents.

Answer: A, C and D only

85470.subject: Zoology
85470.text:
Male frogs can be distinguished from female frogs due to the presence of :
A. Bulging eyes
B. Vocal sacs
C. Webbed digits in feet
D. Copulatory pad on first digit of fore limbs
E. Olive green-coloured skin with dark irregular spots
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
85470.sol:
Male frogs can be distinguished from female frogs by the presence of sound-producing vocal sacs and a copulatory pad on the first digit of the forelimbs. These structures are absent in female frogs.

Bulging eyes, webbed digits in feet, and olive green-coloured skin with dark irregular spots are morphological features common to both male and female frogs.

Therefore, only statements B and D represent the distinguishing features of male frogs.

Answer: B and D only

95748.text:
Read the following statements given about organism formed by association of the phycobiont and mycobiont and identify the true ones.

I. Lichens are mutually beneficial symbiotic associations.

II. They grow extensively in areas with high pollution, hence called as pollution indicators.

III. The phycobiont member, algae, is an autotroph and the mycobiont member, fungi, is a heterotroph.

IV. Fungi helps the algae harvest sunlight for photosynthesis.
95748.sol: Lichens are a symbiotic association of the algae (phycobiont) and fungi (mycobiont). The algal partner produces food and the fungal partner provides protection to the algae. 96962.text: Stem tendrils develop from ________ in plants like gourds.
96962.sol: The stem is a part of a plant consisting of branches, leaves, flowers and fruits. They also exhibit buds which can be axillary or terminal. They perform the function of conducting water, food and minerals and photosynthesis. In some plants, the stem is modified in different structures to perform various functions. 97014.subject: Botany
97014.text: The following diagrams represent the types of aestivation in corolla. Identify the correct combination of labelling.
97014.sol:
The mode of arrangement of sepals or petals in floral bud with respect to the other members of the same whorl is known as aestivation. The main types of aestivation are valvate, twisted, imbricate and vexillary.
In valvate, sepals or petals just touch one another at the margin, without overlapping, e.g., Calotropis.
In twisted, one margin of sepal or petal overlaps that of the next one and so on, e.g., China rose, lady’s finger, cotton, etc.
In imbricate, The margins of sepal or petals overlap one another but not in any particular direction e.g., Cassia, Goldmohur.
In vexillary, the largest posterior petal (vexillum or standard) overlaps two lateral petals (alae or wings) which in turn overlaps the two smallest, anterior but united petals (keel or carina), e.g., pea, bean etc.

100015.subject: Physics
100015.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The mean of three length measurements $4.2 \text{ cm}$, $4.5 \text{ cm}$, and $4.4 \text{ cm}$ is correctly reported as $4.4 \text{ cm}$.
Reason (R): The integer 3 used for division is an exact number with infinite significant figures, so the decimal places in the final result are determined by the addition rule applied to the original measurements.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
100015.sol:
Assertion (A) is true: The sum of the measurements is $4.2 \text{ cm} + 4.5 \text{ cm} + 4.4 \text{ cm} = 13.1 \text{ cm}$. The raw mean is $\dfrac{13.1}{3} = 4.366... \text{ cm}$. Since the original measurements have one decimal place, the mean should also be rounded to one decimal place. Rounding $4.366...$ to one decimal place gives $4.4 \text{ cm}$.

Reason (R) is true and correctly explains the Assertion: When calculating an average, the number of observations (3) is an exact number with infinite significant figures. Therefore, it does not restrict the precision of the result. The precision is governed by the sum of the measurements, which follows the addition rule (retaining the least number of decimal places present in the original data).

Hence, both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

100494.subject: Physics
100494.text: Several particles are executing uniform circular motion. If all of them have the same time period of revolution, which of the following graphs correctly represents the variation of their linear speed ($v$) with the radius ($r$) of their circular paths?
options: A straight line passing through the origin
A straight line parallel to the radius axis
A parabola passing through the origin
100494.sol:
The linear speed $v$ of a particle in uniform circular motion is related to its time period $T$ and radius $r$ by the formula:
$v = \dfrac{2\pi r}{T}$

Since the time period $T$ is constant for all particles, the term $\dfrac{2\pi}{T}$ is a constant.
Therefore, $v \propto r$.

The graph of a directly proportional relationship is a straight line passing through the origin.

Answer: A straight line passing through the origin

101559.subject: Physics
101559.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The compressibility of a material is always a positive quantity.
Reason (R): In the mathematical expression for compressibility, $k = -\dfrac{1}{\Delta P}\left(\dfrac{\Delta V}{V}\right)$, the negative sign accounts for the fact that an increase in pressure results in a decrease in volume.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
101559.sol:
Compressibility is defined as the reciprocal of the bulk modulus of a material. For any stable material, a positive increase in pressure ($\Delta P > 0$) leads to a decrease in volume ($\Delta V < 0$).

To ensure that the bulk modulus and its reciprocal (compressibility) are positive physical quantities, a negative sign is explicitly included in their defining formulas.

Thus, $k = -\dfrac{1}{\Delta P}\left(\dfrac{\Delta V}{V}\right)$ yields a positive value because the negative $\Delta V$ cancels with the negative sign in the formula.

Therefore, both Assertion and Reason are correct, and the Reason correctly explains the Assertion.

101754.text: Two small drops of mercury, each of radius $R$, coalesce to form a single large drop. The ratio of the total surface energies before and after the change is
101754.sol:
Radius of one drop of mercury is $R$.
$\therefore \quad$ The volume of one drop $=\frac{4}{3} \pi R^3\therefore$ Total volume of the two drops,

V=2 $\times \frac{4}{3} \pi$R^3=$\frac{8}{3} \pi$R^3

Let the radius of the large drop formed be $R^{\prime}$.
The volume of the large drop is also $V$.

\therefore \quad $\frac{4}{3} \pi$R^{\prime 3}=$\frac{8}{3} \pi$R^3 \Rightarrow R^{\prime 3}=2 R³ \Rightarrow R^{\prime}=2^{1 / 3} R $\text{. }$Now the surface area of the two drops is

S_1=2 $\times$4 $\pi$R^2=8 $\pi$R^2

and the surface area of the resultant drop is

S_2=4 $\pi$R^{\prime 2}=4 $\pi$2^{2 / 3} R²

Let $T$ be the surface tension of mercury. Therefore the surface energy of the two drops before coalescing is

U_1=S_1 T=8 $\pi$R^2 T

and the surface energy after coalescing,

$\begin{gathered}$U_2=S_2 T=2^{2 / 3} $\times$4 $\pi$R^2 T \\
\therefore \quad $\frac{U_1}{U_2}=\frac{8 \pi R^2 T}{2^{2 / 3} \times 4 \pi R^2 T}=\frac{2}{2^{2 / 3}}=$2^{1 / 3} .
\end{gathered}

102440.subject: Physics
102440.text: Two simple pendulums, $P$ and $Q$, are allowed to oscillate at the same location. It is observed that pendulum $P$ completes $20$ oscillations in the exact same time that pendulum $Q$ completes $30$ oscillations. What is the ratio of the length of pendulum $P$ to the length of pendulum $Q$ ($L_P : L_Q$)?
102440.sol:
Let the time taken for the given number of oscillations be $t$.

The time period of pendulum $P$ is $T_P = \dfrac{t}{20}$.

The time period of pendulum $Q$ is $T_Q = \dfrac{t}{30}$.

The ratio of their time periods is:

$\dfrac{T_P}{T_Q} = \dfrac{\dfrac{t}{20}}{\dfrac{t}{30}} = \dfrac{30}{20} = \dfrac{3}{2}$

The time period of a simple pendulum is given by $T = 2\pi \sqrt{\dfrac{L}{g}}$.

Since $T \propto \sqrt{L}$, we have $L \propto T^2$.

Therefore, the ratio of their lengths is:

$\dfrac{L_P}{L_Q} = \left(\dfrac{T_P}{T_Q}\right)^2 = \left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right)^2 = \dfrac{9}{4}$

Thus, the ratio $L_P : L_Q$ is $9 : 4$.

Answer: $9 : 4$

102457.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): For a particle executing simple harmonic motion, the frequency of its kinetic energy is double the frequency of its displacement.
Reason (R): The total mechanical energy of a particle executing simple harmonic motion is directly proportional to the square of its amplitude.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true
102457.sol:
The assertion is true. For a particle in SHM, displacement is given by $x = A\sin(\omega t)$ and velocity by $v = A\omega\cos(\omega t)$. The kinetic energy is $K = \dfrac{1}{2}mv^2 = \dfrac{1}{2}mA^2\omega^2\cos^2(\omega t)$. Using the trigonometric identity $\cos^2(\theta) = \dfrac{1+\cos(2\theta)}{2}$, the kinetic energy expression contains a $\cos(2\omega t)$ term. This means the angular frequency of kinetic energy is $2\omega$, making its physical frequency double that of the displacement.

The reason is also true. The total mechanical energy of a particle in SHM is $E = \dfrac{1}{2}mA^2\omega^2$, which shows it is directly proportional to the square of the amplitude ($A^2$).

However, the reason states the dependence of total energy on amplitude, which does not explain why the frequency of kinetic energy is doubled. The correct explanation would involve the squared dependence of kinetic energy on the instantaneous sinusoidal velocity. Thus, both statements are true, but the reason is not the correct explanation for the assertion.

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion (A)

102461.subject: Physics
102461.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): For a particle executing simple harmonic motion, the phase difference between its displacement and acceleration is always $\pi$ radians.

Reason (R): In simple harmonic motion, the acceleration is always directly proportional to the negative of the displacement.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion and Reason are correct but Reason is not the correct explanation for Assertion.
Assertion is correct but Reason is incorrect.
Both Assertion and Reason are correct and Reason is the correct explanation for Assertion.
Assertion is incorrect but Reason is correct.
102461.sol:
Assertion (A) is correct: In simple harmonic motion (SHM), if displacement is $x = A \sin(\omega t)$, then velocity is $v = A\omega \cos(\omega t)$ and acceleration is $a = -A\omega^2 \sin(\omega t) = A\omega^2 \sin(\omega t + \pi)$. The phase difference between displacement and acceleration is exactly $\pi$ radians.

Reason (R) is correct: The defining condition for a particle to execute SHM is that its acceleration is directly proportional to the negative of its displacement, i.e., $a = -\omega^2 x$.

Reason (R) is the correct explanation for Assertion (A): The negative sign in the relation $a = -\omega^2 x$ mathematically corresponds to a phase shift of $180^\circ$ (or $\pi$ radians). Therefore, the proportionality to the negative of displacement is the fundamental reason why acceleration and displacement are out of phase by $\pi$ radians.

Answer: Both Assertion and Reason are correct and Reason is the correct explanation for Assertion.

103540.text:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the magnetic susceptibility ($\chi$) and relative permeability ($\mu_r$) of various materials.

List-IList-II
(A) Superconductor(I) $-1 < \chi < 0$ and $0 < \mu_r < 1$
(B) Diamagnetic material(II) $\chi = -1$ and $\mu_r = 0$
(C) Paramagnetic material(III) $\chi \gg 1$ and $\mu_r \gg 1$
(D) Ferromagnetic material(IV) $0 < \chi < \epsilon$ and $\mu_r > 1$ (where $\epsilon$ is a small positive number)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
103540.sol:
Superconductors exhibit the Meissner effect, acting as perfect diamagnets, so $\chi = -1$ and $\mu_r = 0$.

Normal diamagnetic materials have a small negative susceptibility, so $-1 < \chi < 0$ and $0 < \mu_r < 1$.

Paramagnetic materials have a small positive susceptibility, so $0 < \chi < \epsilon$ and $\mu_r > 1$.

Ferromagnetic materials have a very large positive susceptibility, so $\chi \gg 1$ and $\mu_r \gg 1$.

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(III).

Answer: (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(III)

103913.subject: Physics
103913.text: A graph of the induced EMF versus time for a coil rotating in a uniform magnetic field is a sinusoidal curve. From the graph, the peak-to-peak EMF is read as $628 \text{ V}$ and the time for one complete cycle is $0.02 \text{ s}$. If the coil consists of $500$ turns and has a cross-sectional area of $0.1 \text{ m}^2$, what is the magnitude of the uniform magnetic field? (Take $\pi = 3.14$)
103913.sol:
From the described graph, the peak-to-peak EMF is $628 \text{ V}$. The peak (maximum) induced EMF is half of this value:
$E_{max} = \dfrac{628}{2} = 314 \text{ V}$

The time period $T = 0.02 \text{ s}$. The angular velocity $\omega$ is:
$\omega = \dfrac{2\pi}{T} = \dfrac{2 \times 3.14}{0.02} = 314 \text{ rad s}^{-1}$

The maximum induced EMF for a rotating coil is given by:
$E_{max} = NAB\omega$

Substituting the given values ($N = 500$, $A = 0.1 \text{ m}^2$):
$314 = 500 \times 0.1 \times B \times 314$
$1 = 50 \times B$
$B = \dfrac{1}{50} = 0.02 \text{ T}$

Using the peak-to-peak value directly instead of the peak value leads to $0.04 \text{ T}$, while confusing angular velocity with frequency leads to $0.1256 \text{ T}$.

Answer: $0.02 \text{ T}$

105489.text:
Given below are two statements: One is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A) : In Davisson-Germer experiment wavelength associated with the beam decreases with increases of speed of electrons.
Reason (R) : Wavelength associated with electron beam in Davission-Germer experiment is given by \(\lambda=\frac{\mathrm{h}}{\sqrt{2 \mathrm{mK}}}\)
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is NOT the correct explanation of \((\mathrm{A})\).
105489.sol:
To analyze the statements:
Assertion (A): "In Davisson-Germer experiment, the wavelength associated with the beam decreases with an increase in the speed of electrons."
- This statement is true. According to de Broglie's hypothesis, the wavelength \(\lambda\) is inversely proportional to the momentum \(p\) of the particle, which is related to its speed. As the speed of electrons increases, the wavelength decreases.
Reason (R): "Wavelength associated with the electron beam in Davisson-Germer experiment is given by \(\lambda=\frac{h}{\sqrt{2 m K}}\)."
- This statement is also true. The formula given represents the de Broglie wavelength for particles, where \(h\) is Planck's constant, \(m\) is the mass of the electron, and \(K\) is the kinetic energy.

105582.subject: Physics
105582.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): If the frequency of incident light is less than the threshold frequency, halving the distance between a point light source and a photoelectric metal will not produce any photoelectric current.

Reason (R): The intensity of light from a point source is inversely proportional to the square of the distance from the source.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
105582.sol:
Assertion (A) is true: For photoelectric emission to occur, the incident frequency must be strictly greater than the threshold frequency ($ u > u_0$). If $ u < u_0$, no emission takes place, and the photoelectric current remains zero regardless of the intensity of the incident light.

Reason (R) is true: For a point source, intensity $I \propto \dfrac{1}{r^2}$. Halving the distance increases the intensity by four times.

However, (R) is not the correct explanation of (A). The correct explanation for (A) is that the energy of individual photons ($h u$) is less than the work function of the metal, so they cannot eject electrons, even though the total number of incident photons per unit area per unit time (intensity) has increased.

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

107027.subject: Chemistry
107027.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
107027.text: The correct decreasing order of atomic radii for Oxygen (O), Fluorine (F), and Neon (Ne) is:
107027.sol:
Oxygen, Fluorine, and Neon belong to the second period of the periodic table.

Generally, atomic radius decreases from left to right across a period due to an increase in effective nuclear charge. Therefore, the covalent radius of Oxygen is greater than that of Fluorine ($\mathrm{O} \gt \mathrm{F}$).

However, Neon is a noble gas. Noble gases do not form covalent molecules under normal conditions, so their atomic radii are expressed as van der Waals radii. Van der Waals radii are non-bonded radii and are significantly larger than the covalent radii of the preceding elements in the same period.

Thus, Neon has the largest atomic radius among the three. The correct decreasing order is $\mathrm{Ne} \gt \mathrm{O} \gt \mathrm{F}$.

Answer: $\mathrm{Ne} \gt \mathrm{O} \gt \mathrm{F}$

108665.subject: Chemistry
108665.text:
Consider the dimerization of nitrogen dioxide gas into dinitrogen tetroxide gas:
$2\mathrm{NO}_{2(\mathrm{g})} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{N}_2\mathrm{O}_{4(\mathrm{g})}$

Which of the following correctly describes the signs of enthalpy change ($\Delta H$) and entropy change ($\Delta S$) for this process, and the temperature condition for its spontaneity?
options: $\Delta H < 0$, $\Delta S < 0$; spontaneous at high temperatures
$\Delta H > 0$, $\Delta S > 0$; spontaneous at high temperatures
$\Delta H < 0$, $\Delta S < 0$; spontaneous at low temperatures
$\Delta H < 0$, $\Delta S > 0$; spontaneous at all temperatures
108665.sol:
In the dimerization process, $2\mathrm{NO}_{2(\mathrm{g})} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{N}_2\mathrm{O}_{4(\mathrm{g})}$, a new N-N bond is formed without breaking any existing bonds. Bond formation releases energy, so the process is exothermic ($\Delta H < 0$).

The number of gaseous moles decreases from 2 to 1 ($\Delta n_g = -1$), which means the randomness of the system decreases, so $\Delta S < 0$.

According to the Gibbs free energy equation, $\Delta G = \Delta H - T\Delta S$.

For the reaction to be spontaneous, $\Delta G$ must be negative. Since both $\Delta H$ and $\Delta S$ are negative, $\Delta G$ will be negative only when the magnitude of $\Delta H$ is greater than $T\Delta S$, which occurs at low temperatures.

Answer: $\Delta H < 0$, $\Delta S < 0$; spontaneous at low temperatures

113877.subject: Chemistry
113877.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): A mixture of nitric acid and water forms a maximum boiling azeotrope at a specific composition.

Reason (R): In a mixture of nitric acid and water, the intermolecular acid-water interactions are stronger than the acid-acid and water-water interactions.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
113877.sol:
Assertion (A) is true: A mixture of nitric acid and water (68% nitric acid and 32% water by mass) forms a maximum boiling azeotrope.

Reason (R) is true: Nitric acid and water form a non-ideal solution that shows a negative deviation from Raoult's law. This occurs because the intermolecular interactions between the unlike molecules (acid and water) are stronger than those between the like molecules (acid-acid and water-water).

Because the interactions are stronger, the escaping tendency of the molecules decreases, leading to a lower vapour pressure. A lower vapour pressure means the solution must be heated to a higher temperature to boil, which perfectly explains the formation of a maximum boiling azeotrope.

Therefore, both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

113907.subject: Chemistry
113907.text:
Match List I with List II :

List IList II
A. MolarityI. Temperature independent
B. MolalityII. Temperature dependent
C. Bends in scuba diversIII. Decreased gas solubility due to low pressure
D. Anoxia at high altitudesIV. Increased gas solubility due to high pressure

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
113907.sol:
Molarity is defined as the number of moles of solute per litre of solution. Since the volume of a liquid changes with temperature, molarity is temperature dependent. (A-II)

Molality is defined as the number of moles of solute per kg of solvent. Since mass does not change with temperature, molality is temperature independent. (B-I)

Bends in scuba divers occur because the high pressure underwater increases the solubility of atmospheric gases (like nitrogen) in the blood. When the diver surfaces, the pressure decreases, releasing the dissolved gases as bubbles. (C-IV)

Anoxia at high altitudes is a condition caused by the low atmospheric pressure, which leads to a decreased solubility of oxygen in the blood and tissues, causing weakness and inability to think clearly. (D-III)

Therefore, the correct matching is A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III.

Answer: A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III

114346.subject: Chemistry
114346.text: The limiting molar conductivities of $\text{Ba(OH)}_2$, $\text{BaCl}_2$ and $\text{NH}_4\text{Cl}$ are given as $x$, $y$ and $z \text{ S cm}^2 \text{ mol}^{-1}$ respectively. The limiting molar conductivity of $\text{NH}_4\text{OH}$ in $\text{S cm}^2 \text{ mol}^{-1}$ will be:
114346.sol:
According to Kohlrausch's law of independent migration of ions:

$\Lambda_m^0(\text{Ba(OH)}_2) = \lambda^0_{\text{Ba}^{2+}} + 2\lambda^0_{\text{OH}^-} = x$
$\Lambda_m^0(\text{BaCl}_2) = \lambda^0_{\text{Ba}^{2+}} + 2\lambda^0_{\text{Cl}^-} = y$
$\Lambda_m^0(\text{NH}_4\text{Cl}) = \lambda^0_{\text{NH}_4^+} + \lambda^0_{\text{Cl}^-} = z$

Subtracting the second equation from the first gives:
$x - y = 2\lambda^0_{\text{OH}^-} - 2\lambda^0_{\text{Cl}^-}$
$\Rightarrow \lambda^0_{\text{OH}^-} - \lambda^0_{\text{Cl}^-} = \dfrac{x - y}{2}$

The limiting molar conductivity for $\text{NH}_4\text{OH}$ is:
$\Lambda_m^0(\text{NH}_4\text{OH}) = \lambda^0_{\text{NH}_4^+} + \lambda^0_{\text{OH}^-}$

This can be rewritten as:
$\Lambda_m^0(\text{NH}_4\text{OH}) = (\lambda^0_{\text{NH}_4^+} + \lambda^0_{\text{Cl}^-}) + (\lambda^0_{\text{OH}^-} - \lambda^0_{\text{Cl}^-})$
$\Lambda_m^0(\text{NH}_4\text{OH}) = z + \dfrac{x - y}{2}$

Answer: $\dfrac{x - y}{2} + z$

121561.subject: Botany
121561.text: A biologist observes an organism forming extensive blooms in a highly polluted water body. Upon further analysis, the organism is found to be a photosynthetic autotroph possessing chlorophyll $a$ similar to green plants. Which of the following statements is true regarding this organism?
options: It belongs to Archaebacteria and possesses a different cell wall structure for survival in extreme conditions.
It is a Eubacterium and some of its members possess specialised cells called heterocysts for nitrogen fixation.
It is a chemosynthetic autotroph that oxidises various inorganic substances to recycle nutrients.
It is a methanogen that survives in aquatic environments and produces biogas.
121561.sol:
The organism described forms blooms in polluted water bodies and possesses chlorophyll $a$ similar to green plants. These features are characteristic of Cyanobacteria (blue-green algae).

Cyanobacteria belong to the group Eubacteria (true bacteria). Some members of Cyanobacteria, such as Nostoc and Anabaena, have specialised cells called heterocysts that help in fixing atmospheric nitrogen.

They are not Archaebacteria, nor are they chemosynthetic autotrophs (which oxidise inorganic substances) or methanogens (which are Archaebacteria found in marshy areas or ruminant guts).

Answer: It is a Eubacterium and some of its members possess specialised cells called heterocysts for nitrogen fixation.

122564.text: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes members of Class Cyclostomata from members of Class Chondrichthyes?

Cyclostomes lack scales on their body, whereas Chondrichthyes possess tough skin with minute placoid scales.
122564.sol:
Members of Class Cyclostomata (Division Agnatha) are jawless vertebrates whose bodies are devoid of scales and paired fins. In contrast, members of Class Chondrichthyes (Division Gnathostomata) have powerful jaws, paired fins, and tough skin containing minute placoid scales.

The other options are incorrect because both Cyclostomata and Chondrichthyes possess a cartilaginous endoskeleton (cranium and vertebral column) and both have a closed type of circulatory system. Furthermore, it is Chondrichthyes that possess paired fins, while Cyclostomes lack them.

Answer: Cyclostomes lack scales on their body, whereas Chondrichthyes possess tough skin with minute placoid scales.

123251.subject: Botany
123251.text: Identify X and select the correct statement.
options: Subsidiary cells - A few guard cells, in the vicinity of the epidermal cells become specialized in their shape and size and are known as subsidiary cells
Epidermal cells - Epidermal cells are sclerenchymatous with a small amount of cytoplasm lining the cell wall and a large vacuole
Guard cells - The guard cells possess chloroplasts and regulate the opening and closing of stomata
123251.sol: Epidermal cells are parenchymatous with a small amount of cytoplasm lining the cell wall and a large vacuole. The outside of the epidermis is often covered with a waxy thick layer called the cuticle which prevents the loss of water. Cuticle is absent in roots. Stomata are structures present in the epidermis of leaves. Stomata regulate the process of transpiration and gaseous exchange. Each stoma is composed of two bean shaped cells known as guard cells which enclose stomatal pore. In grasses, the guard cells are dumb-bell shaped. The outer walls of guard cells (away from the stomatal pore) are thin and the inner walls (towards the stomatal pore) are highly thickened. The guard cells possess chloroplasts and regulate the opening and closing of stomata. Sometimes, a few epidermal cells, in the vicinity of the guard cells become specialised in their shape and size and are known as subsidiary cells.
